summary: @nebula.js/theme preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is an obfuscated script (obfuscator.io-style _0x-named identifiers and dispatch-object control flow) that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, sets it executable, and uses it to run a bundled sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync. math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated JavaScript bundle (large numeric string-array table with function-permutation dispatch, e.g. WV8StW), delivered under the '// @bun @bun-cjs' header so it runs under the freshly downloaded Bun runtime rather than Node. The alternate-runtime-dropper shape moves execution outside Node-based tooling visibility. The package presents itself as '@nebula.js/theme' with author 'QlikTech International AB' — a namespace matching Qlik's real nebula.js packages — but the upstream Qlik theme library has no such preinstall step and no Bun dependency. package.json declares files: ['dist'], yet setup.mjs and math_init.js are smuggled into the tarball root outside that allowlist. On npm install, arbitrary attacker-controlled code from math_init.js executes on the installer's host under a runtime the package fetched itself.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
